question.text: This Canadian province held sovereignty referendums in 1980 and 1995 because many of its residents want to become an independent country. Unlike residents in other provinces, most of its residents speak French.
question.clue: Following a crisis in this region, the War Measures Act was invoked by a Prime Minister who said "just watch me", Pierre Trudeau.

swap.text: The younger Trudeau replaced this Conservative as PM in 2015. He withdrew Canada from the Kyoto Protocol and slashed Canada's taxes early in his tenure to a lower corporate rate than the U.S.
swap.clue: This man led the National Citizen Coalition, a conservative lobbyist group. This former Canadian Prime Minister was succeeded by Trudeau in the late 2015 elections.

question.text: A Quebecois ["que-beck-WAA"] prime minister of Canada with this last name invoked the War Measures Act for the third time in history to end the October Crisis. His son with this surname won a third term as Canadian prime minister in 2021 federal elections.
question.answerHtml: Trudeau [accept Pierre Trudeau or Joseph Philippe Pierre Yves Elliot Trudeau or Justin Trudeau or Justin Pierre James Trudeau]
question.clue: Another politician with this name initiated the Phoenix Pay system, and was given the nickname "little potato" when attending a G20 summit in China.

swap.leadin: Name the following Canadian Prime Ministers.
swap.text: This Liberal served in the role for 22 years over three disjoint lengths of time; he was Prime Minister throughout the entirety of World War II.
swap.answerHtml: William Lyon Mackenzie King (prompt on partial answer)
swap.clue: Following a scandal involving one of his customs officials named Jacques Bureau, this man tried to get around a proposal put forth by W. R. Fansher that would have censured his government by calling for a new election, but Governor General Lord Byng refused.

question.leadin: This man was accused of metaphorically urinating on a rug after giving a speech in Philadelphia in 1965 where he questioned U.S. foreign policy.
question.text: Name this Canadian prime minister, who earlier won a Nobel Peace Prize for negotiating an end to the Suez Crisis.
question.clue: This politician claimed "Canadians do not need to be liberated" in response to the "Vive le Quebec Libre" speech another man gave at Expo 67.

swap.leadin: Name the following, about the colonization of North America.
swap.text: This French explorer named Canada after the Iroquois word for "settlement."
swap.clue: On their second voyage, this person made contact with the residents of the village of Stadacona.

question.text: The nickname "Old Ironsides" came from now-captain Isaac Hull's victory over the Guerriere at the start of the War of 1812. The Guerriere had been heading for this British Atlantic port, now the capital of Nova Scotia.
question.clue: During the French and Indian War, the British army kept prisoners on Georges Island in this city's harbor.

swap.text: Both Anthony Eden and his successor Harold Macmillan were members of this British political party. Notable Hitler-appeaser Neville Chamberlain was also a member of this party.
swap.clue: One member of this party cited an old woman who refused to lease to immigrants in his Rivers of Blood speech.

question.text: He kept appointed governor William McDougall from entering the Red River settlement and won favorable terms in the Manitoba Act. For 15 points, name this leader of the Metis who led a revolt of French-speaking Indian descendants against Canadian rule.
question.clue: This man was captured with the Cree Chief Poundmaker during the Battle of Batoche, and he appointed a tribunal which sentenced Thomas Scott to death.

swap.leadin: This politician oversaw the passage of the Charter of Rights and Freedoms.
swap.text: Name this politician who ran on the notion of a "Just Society" in one election, and lost power to Joe Clark's Progressive Conservatives for one year.
swap.clue: After the death of Pierre Laporte, this man told reporters "just watch me" following his invocation of the War Measures Act during the October Crisis.

question.text: Under King, Canada saw a 1926 constitutional crisis when Julian Byng, who held this office, refused King's request to dissolve Parliament and hold new elections. This office represents the English monarchy in Canada.
question.clue: In 1952, Vincent Massey became the first holder of this position to not be a member of the peerage.

swap.text: The end of the North-West Rebellion came in the Battle of Loon Lake, which featured insurgents defeated by members of this Canadian police force, noted for their distinctive red uniforms.
swap.answerHtml: Royal Canadian Mounted Police [or the Royal North-West Mounted Police or the Mounties, or RCMP, or NWMP, or RNWMP]
swap.clue: 250 members of this organization maintained order during an 1890s gold rush.

question.text: The Patriotes' 1837 rebellion against British rule occurred in this North American colony. This colony, which comprised present-day Quebec, was later unified with an oppositely named colony corresponding to Ontario.

swap.leadin: This city was founded on site of the Indian village of Stadacona.
swap.text: This Canadian settlement, the capital of New France, was founded by Samuel de Champlain, along with Montreal. During the French and Indian War, General Wolfe died on the Plains of Abraham outside this city.
swap.answerHtml: City of Quebec [or Quebec City; or Ville de Québec]

question.leadin: These people may have inspired the tuniit("toon-EAT"), a race of giants in a successor culture's mythology.
question.text: Name this archaeological culture, which preceded the Thule people in northern Canada and Greenland. Bows and arrows are conspicuously absent from their sites despite their use by the previous Saqqaq ("sah-KAHK") culture.
question.clue: X-shaped incisions on figures' heads from this culture have been linked to shamanistic travels.

swap.text: The Yupik peoples and these people of the Arctic and Subarctic were direct descendants of the Thule peoples. These indigenous people identified the Dorset as giants that they call the Tuniit.
swap.answerHtml: Inuit [accept Inupiat or Iñupiaq; accept Eskimo but inform the player that the term is considered offensive]
swap.clue: In the 1950s, this ethnic group's dogs were killed by the RCMP.

question.text: This Liberal Prime Minister from 1948-57 enthusiastically got Canada on board NATO, expanded social security, and directed his Secretary of State for External Affairs, Lester Pearson, to resolve the Suez Crisis.
question.answerHtml: Louis St. Laurent [or Louis Stephen St. Laurent; or Louis-Etienne St-Laurent]
question.clue: This Canadian Prime Minister preceded John Diefenbaker. This Prime Minister helped establish NATO, while his foreign affairs minister Lester Pearson helped broker the Suez Crisis.

swap.leadin: During the Cold War, the governments of Canada and the United States historically operated this defensive line of radar stations.
swap.text: Name this line of stations at sites including Point Lay, Alaska and Alert, Nunavut. Either the three-word name or the three-letter acronym they are more commonly known by are acceptable.

question.text: This Canadian Prime Minister attended the joint funeral for nine of the women killed in the massacre. This man met with Ronald Reagan at the infamous "Shamrock Summit."
question.clue: He replaced the Manufacturer's Tax with the Goods and Services Tax and passed an agreement that opponents like Ed Broadbent claimed would turn into the 51st state, the Free Trade Agreement.

swap.leadin: This rebellion began with the defeat of Leif Crozier by troops under Gabriel Dumont at Duck Lake.
swap.text: Name this Metis rebellion in Saskatchewan that ended at the Battle of Batoche. The Cree Indians Poundmaker and Big Bear were part of this rebellion.
swap.answerHtml: North-West Rebellion [or Saskatchewan Rebellion; or Northwest Uprising; or Second Riel Rebellion]
